primary_task: Target for this guided_b session: Practice revision with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support. Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of revision. Check, revise, or improve work about revision using stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about revision; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. What revision means here: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable. How the relationship changes the result: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect. 1. Guided practice: Begin the second pass on revision with the earlier model and cue closed. Make two new studies, compare them with the first supported pass, and report whether the previously fragile move now holds without the prompt. 2. Independent transfer: Transfer revision to a third, unfamiliar case without reopening the scaffold. Revisit the move marked fragile in the first pass and cite the independent evidence that shows whether it now works. 3. Critique: Describe before judging. Locate evidence, compare it with the maker’s stated intent, ask one genuine question, and offer options; the maker keeps final authority. A private self-critique receives full credit. 4. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. Your choices remain yours: Different medium, subject or source material, sequence, criterion to test, final revision choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about revision. It is part of "Materials, Techniques, and Design". Later days in this unit cover other things, like drawing tools. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about revision; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for revision fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.
sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g5-arts-and-music-u02-l06

Lesson focus: revision

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD B — support-fading pass for revision. Earlier-pass substitute: Short → short-short → long can be drawn, tapped, moved, or silently counted while preserving its pattern of arrival, urgency, and rest. Mark the relationship involving sequence as the fragile move, then hide this resource. Make two new studies, loops, maps, or responses without the prompt. Reopen only afterward; compare the order of decisions and the evidence. Report whether the fragile move held. If it did not, use the criteria to name the mismatch without changing the learner’s intent or copying the example. Use it to study revision; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.fallback: Use the complete adjacent verbal description and recreate the relationships with raised or movable paper forms. The required Academy model is attached; no outside search is needed.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce revision to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one sequence relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact sequence evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply revision under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on revision rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one sequence relationship while working on revision.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.

age_policy.language: Scannable steps with reasons for the main artistic choices.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

concept_instruction.title: What revision means here
concept_instruction.body: An artistic relationship can be tested across more than one medium when the same structure—such as repetition, contrast, or sequence—remains observable.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: Moving between media can reveal structure but may change the measured skill; name which evidence transfers and which does not. Worked example: Short → short-short → long can be drawn, tapped, moved, or silently counted while preserving its pattern of arrival, urgency, and rest. Non-example: Switching media and changing every relationship at once makes it impossible to tell what caused the new effect.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in revision.
technique_sequence.why: Changing one feature while preserving the others reveals what that feature contributes to the intended effect.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for revision is present, but the record does not yet locate sequence, repetition, spacing, duration, scale, contrast, transition, and stated intent that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
